Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the GlobalTech Semiconductor Corp. Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today's call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Ms. Emily Carter, Investor Relations Director. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter, Investor Relations Director:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and welcome to GlobalTech Semiconductor Corp.’s second quarter earnings call. Joining me today are Dr. James Lee, CEO; Mr. David Chen, CFO; and Dr. Anya Sharma, Chief Technology Officer.
Earlier today, we published our earnings press release and slides, which are available on our IR site. Please note this call may contain forward-looking statements. Now, I’ll turn it over to Dr. Lee.

James Lee, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Emily. Hello, everyone.

Let’s start with a look at the quarter:

We made strong progress this quarter. Our consolidated gross margin for Q2 reached approximately 36%, translating to TWD 20.25 billion. This represents a slight improvement compared to the 35.4% we achieved in Q1 2024, where the gross profit was TWD 19.15 billion. Cumulatively, for the first six months of the year, our gross margin stands at 35.7%, representing a total gross profit of TWD 39.4 billion. While seemingly modest, this improvement reflects a complex interplay of factors.

We also saw great momentum in securing design wins with three key customers this quarter, all focused on developing cutting-edge AI accelerators. This quarter marks a significant milestone in our foundry business, driven by strategic design wins leveraging our advanced silicon interposer technology, particularly within the high-growth AI accelerator market.

These achievements underscore our commitment to disciplined execution and innovation.

Now I’ll pass it to David to walk through in more detail.

David Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, James, and hello, everyone.

Let me take you through the financials:

First, building on what James said, we’ve continued to drive improvements there, specifically in our foundry business. We secured design wins with a major hyperscaler, a leading AI chip startup, and a government research institution. The hyperscaler selected our interposer technology for their next-generation in-house AI accelerator. The design win encompasses a multi-year agreement with projected revenue exceeding $750 million over the next five years. The AI chip startup chose our interposer technology to enable the integration of multiple high-bandwidth memory stacks alongside their AI processing cores. And the government research institution awarded us a contract to provide interposer technology for advanced AI research focused on national security applications.

We invested strategically in the new fab construction area, resulting in significant advancements in the construction phase of our new fabrication facility, designated P3. Q3 2024 saw us successfully complete the structural build-out, including the cleanroom shell, ahead of schedule and under budget. This represents a critical milestone, enabling us to accelerate the tool move-in process. The P3 construction project remains within its allocated budget of $12.5 billion.

Additionally, we’ve seen progress in net margin and diluted EPS. Our analysis of GlobalTech Semiconductor Corp’s Q2 2023 and first-half (H1) 2023 results reveals a generally positive picture. Net income attributable to the stockholder of the parent company reached TWD 15.6 billion in Q2, translating to a diluted EPS of TWD 1.27. H1 2023 saw a total net income of TWD 32.2 billion, a net income rate (net margin) of 29.2%, and a diluted EPS of TWD 2.58. We believe this demonstrates solid profitability on a per-share basis.

Now I’ll turn it over to Anya, who will speak about operations and innovation.

Anya Sharma, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, David.

Let me begin with a closer look at the gross margin performance, particularly on the factors driving the improvements. The 60-basis point (0.6%) improvement in gross margin from Q1 to Q2 is primarily attributable to increased sales volume in high-margin product lines, especially our AI accelerator chips, as well as supply chain optimization efficiencies, favorable currency exchange rates, and reduced scrap and rework costs. Compared to Q2 2023, when our gross margin was 34.5%, we have witnessed a more substantial improvement of 150 basis points (1.5%), driven by a strategic shift towards higher-value, higher-margin products and services, increased automation, strategic pricing adjustments, and strong regional performance, especially in North America. In our Q1 2024 earnings call, we guided for a gross margin of approximately 35.5% for Q2. Our actual performance of 36% exceeded this guidance by 50 basis points, attributed to stronger-than-expected demand for AI chips, successful execution of cost reduction initiatives, conservative forecasting, and the unforeseen positive impact from new technology implementation. We introduced a new AI-powered tool to predict and proactively resolve manufacturing bottlenecks, and it’s already contributing to improved throughput.

I’d also like to expand on our CapEx guidance. Our full-year 2023 Capital Expenditure (CapEx) guidance for the foundry business remains firmly at $3.0 billion. While we are holding firm on the overall figure, there have been some internal shifts in allocation. We front-loaded approximately 60% of our CapEx spending into the first half of the year. Due to permitting delays and logistical challenges encountered in the Arizona expansion project, we have reallocated approximately $150 million from the North American budget to accelerate the build-out of our advanced packaging capabilities in Singapore. We anticipate a slightly lower CapEx spend in Q3, around $500 million, with the remaining $700 million allocated to Q4.

Let’s move to the Q&A.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
You mentioned strong improvements in net margin and Diluted EPS. Can you talk more about what's driving the slight deceleration in EPS growth from Q1 to Q2?

David Chen:
Certainly. While the H1 net margin is healthy, it's crucial to examine the quarterly trend. The slight deceleration in EPS growth from Q1 to Q2 suggests a possible marginal compression in the net margin. This could be due to increased input costs, a shift in revenue mix towards lower-margin products like our legacy 28nm chips, and increased operating expenses associated with the development of our next-generation Xenon-A chip architecture. We also need to consider the potential impact of share dilution, currency fluctuations, and tax rate variations. However, we remain confident in our ability to manage these factors and maintain strong profitability.

Analyst 2:
Can you elaborate on the trajectory of the new fab construction progress and the anticipated timeline for volume production?

Anya Sharma:
Sure. Q3 2024 saw significant advancements in the construction phase of our new fabrication facility, designated P3. We successfully completed the structural build-out, including the cleanroom shell, ahead of schedule and under budget. Tool move-in commenced in late August, focusing initially on the metrology and inspection equipment. ASML has successfully delivered and installed two of the three planned EUV lithography systems. We are leveraging robotic automation extensively in the BEOL area to improve efficiency and reduce potential contamination. We remain on track for P3 to enter volume production by mid-2025.

Analyst 3:
With regard to the foundry customer design wins, how does the silicon interposer technology give you a competitive advantage?

David Chen:
Our success in securing these design wins hinges on our differentiated interposer technology. It enables extremely high interconnect densities, supporting complex chiplet architectures and maximizing data throughput between processing cores and memory. Our interposer designs incorporate advanced thermal management features, allowing customers to push the performance limits of their AI accelerators without compromising reliability. Our technology facilitates the seamless integration of diverse chiplets, including CPUs, GPUs, and specialized AI accelerators, into a single package. To meet the anticipated surge in demand, we are investing $1.2 billion in upgrading our existing fabrication facilities and building a new state-of-the-art advanced packaging line dedicated to interposer production.

Closing

James Lee:
Thank you all for joining us today. We're energized by the momentum we’re seeing and look forward to sharing continued progress next quarter.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes the call. You may now disconnect.
